title: JavaScript in the browser
summary: Run a small script and trace what the browser actually does.
points: HTML gives a page meaning, CSS styles it, and JavaScript responds to data and actions.
Create app.js and connect it with <script src="app.js" defer></script>. A deferred external classic script runs after HTML parsing.
Use console.log to inspect a value. A breakpoint pauses at a line so you can inspect variables and step through execution.
Identifiers are case-sensitive: task and Task are different names.
Read the first error and its file/line number. Use the Network panel when a script fails to load. Fix syntax errors before debugging later behavior.

rows: Run an external classic script after parsing

mistake: Editing a file without saving or refreshing does not update the page you are testing.
challenge: Connect app.js to your planner, log its title, set a breakpoint, and inspect course. Then misspell its name and locate the error.

title: Values, variables & operators
summary: Represent a task using values with clear types.
points: Use const when a binding will not be reassigned and let when it will. const does not freeze an object.
Strings hold text; numbers support arithmetic; booleans are true or false. null is an intentional empty value; undefined often means no value was provided.
Prefer === for equality without type conversion. Assignment with = changes a binding instead of comparing it.
Form input values are strings. Convert deliberately with Number and check Number.isFinite; a blank string converts to zero, so check blank input separately.
Template literals use backticks and ${...} for expressions. + joins strings when an operand is a string; it is not always addition.
mistake: "25" + 5 produces "255". Convert the input before doing arithmetic.
challenge: Read a duration string, reject blank or nonpositive input, convert it, and print a sentence using a template literal.

diagram.caption: Represent a task using values with clear types.

title: Conditions & loops
summary: Choose a path and repeat work without losing control.
points: An if statement runs its block only when its condition is truthy; else supplies the alternative.
false, 0, an empty string, null, undefined, and NaN are falsy. Empty arrays and objects are truthy.
Use for...of for values in an iterable such as an array. for...in visits enumerable property keys and is usually the wrong choice for array values.
A while loop must eventually change the condition or break. Check the stopping rule before running it.
break exits the current loop; continue skips to its next iteration. Keep each branch small enough to trace.
mistake: Using <= array.length in an index loop visits one index past the last element.
challenge: Loop over study durations, ignore zero or negative entries, and count how many sessions meet a 20-minute target.

diagram.title: Conditions & loops
diagram.caption: Choose a path and repeat work without losing control.

title: Functions & scope
summary: Give repeated logic a name and a clear contract.
points: A function takes parameters and can return a value. Arguments are the actual values supplied at a call.
return ends that invocation. A function without an explicit returned value evaluates to undefined.
let and const are block-scoped. A name declared inside a function is not automatically available outside it.
Arrow functions can return one expression implicitly. A body in braces needs return when a result is required.
A closure can retain access to its surrounding lexical variables. For beginner code, prefer explicit parameters over hidden changing state.
mistake: console.log displays a value but does not replace returning it to the caller.
challenge: Write a function that accepts a task title, trims it, and returns whether it contains 1–120 characters. Try valid, blank, and long values.

diagram.title: Functions & scope
diagram.caption: Give repeated logic a name and a clear contract.

title: Arrays & objects
summary: Keep task data separate from how it appears on screen.
points: An array holds an ordered sequence. Its first index is zero; length counts elements, not the final index.
An object groups named properties. Access a fixed key with dot notation or a computed key with brackets.
map transforms each element into a new array. filter keeps elements that pass a predicate; find returns the first match or undefined.
push mutates an array; spread creates a new outer array. Object spread is shallow, so nested objects can still be shared.
Give tasks stable IDs. Array indexes change after filtering or deletion and should not identify a task permanently.
mistake: Changing a nested object inside a shallow copy can also change the original nested object.
challenge: Create three tasks, derive unfinished titles, and toggle one task by its ID using map and object spread.

diagram.title: Arrays & objects
diagram.caption: Keep task data separate from how it appears on screen.

title: DOM & safe rendering
summary: Turn data into accessible page content.
points: The DOM is the browser’s object representation of a document. querySelector returns the first match or null.
Use createElement to construct an element and append to place it in the document.
Use textContent for task titles and other plain user text. innerHTML interprets markup and must not receive untrusted text.
Change classes with classList rather than rebuilding a whole class string unnecessarily.
Preserve meaningful HTML and keyboard access while updating a page. Keep application state separate from DOM text.
output: The list gains one item displaying Review <functions> literally, including its angle brackets.
mistake: Injecting a task title through innerHTML can turn learner text into active markup.
challenge: Render two task titles, including hello, as plain text. Inspect the DOM to confirm no b element was created from the title.

diagram.title: DOM & safe rendering
diagram.caption: Turn data into accessible page content.

title: Events & forms
summary: Respond to keyboard and pointer actions through the same form.
points: addEventListener registers a callback for an event. Pass the function; do not call it while registering.
Listen to submit on the form so pressing Enter and clicking its submit button use the same logic.
preventDefault cancels the default action when the event is cancelable; it does not stop propagation.
event.target is where an event originated. event.currentTarget is the element whose listener is running.
Read .value for text inputs and .checked for checkboxes. Trim and validate input; keep labels, focus, and understandable feedback. Browser validation does not replace server validation.
output: Submitting a nonblank title logs its trimmed text without navigating away. This example only logs; adding and saving tasks are later steps.
mistake: A click listener on a decorative div does not provide native button keyboard behavior.
challenge: Add a labelled title field and submit button. Test Enter, whitespace-only text, and moving focus back to the field after success.

diagram.caption: Respond to keyboard and pointer actions through the same form.

title: Modules & debugging
summary: Split responsibilities and find errors at their source.
points: export exposes a value from a module; import names the exported value and its source file.
Load the entry file using <script type="module" src="app.js"></script>. Module scripts are deferred by default.
In a browser, use explicit relative paths such as ./tasks.js. Serve the project over HTTP; opening file:// URLs can fail for modules.
Modules have their own scope and run in strict mode. Imported bindings cannot be reassigned by the importing module.
Use the first stack-trace location in your code and a breakpoint to find a failed assumption. Check file paths and response MIME types when an import fails.
output:
Learn modules
These are two separate files. Serve their folder over HTTP and load app.js as a module.
mistake: The import path and exported name must match exactly; browser file paths can be case-sensitive.
challenge: Move your title validation into tasks.js and import it from app.js. Break the filename once and diagnose the failed request.

diagram.title: Modules & debugging
diagram.caption: Split responsibilities and find errors at their source.

title: Promises & async/await
summary: Wait for work while keeping failure and cleanup visible.
points: A promise represents eventual fulfillment or rejection. It is not the completed result itself.
An async function always returns a promise. await pauses that function until the promise settles, without blocking all browser activity.
Use try/catch around awaited work that can reject. finally is useful for cleanup such as restoring a disabled control.
Ordinary statements run synchronously. Promise callbacks run after the current synchronous work; await does not make every operation parallel.
Handle success, loading, and failure explicitly. For independent requests Promise.all can wait for them together, but rejects when an input promise rejects.
mistake: A try/catch does not catch a later rejection from a promise you neither await nor otherwise handle.
challenge: Write an async function using Promise.reject, show a friendly failure message in catch, and reset a loading flag in finally.

diagram.title: Promises & async/await
diagram.caption: Wait for work while keeping failure and cleanup visible.

title: Fetch, JSON & failures
summary: Read data with honest loading and failure states.
points: fetch starts an HTTP request and resolves to a Response when a response is available.
Check response.ok before reading the body. HTTP errors such as 404 do not automatically reject the fetch promise.
response.json() is asynchronous. JSON parsing can fail, and valid JSON can still have the wrong shape.
Validate the data your UI needs. For a same-origin learning example, fetch a local sample.json file rather than depending on a third-party service.
A network failure or blocked cross-origin request needs a recovery message. CORS permission comes from the server; no-cors does not make a readable JSON API response.
output: With a sample.json body of ["Read", "Practice"], logs 2. Failed requests, invalid JSON, or non-array data show the recovery message.
mistake: A 404 response can reach the success path unless you explicitly check response.ok.
challenge: Load a local JSON list with a loading indicator. Test an empty list, malformed JSON, and a missing file; restore the button in finally.

diagram.title: Fetch, JSON & failures
diagram.caption: Read data with honest loading and failure states.

title: Local storage & recovery
summary: Remember small amounts of task data without promising cloud sync.
points: localStorage stores strings for an origin. Use JSON.stringify and JSON.parse for structured data.
Data can survive reloads on the same browser profile, but storage can be blocked, cleared, or unavailable. Catch read and write errors.
Validate parsed data before using it. Old or edited stored values can have an unexpected shape.
Use a namespaced, versioned key. removeItem deletes that key; clear removes all keys for the origin and may erase unrelated app data.
Local storage is neither an account nor a secure vault. Do not put passwords or private tokens in a learning planner. Data does not sync across devices.
output: Review, when storage is available. Otherwise the message explains that storage could not be used. This example writes only its dedicated learning key.
mistake: Calling localStorage.clear() to reset one feature can remove data belonging to other features on the same origin.
challenge: Save a small task array using a dedicated key. Reload, try malformed stored JSON, and show an explicit recovery option rather than silently overwriting it.

diagram.title: Local storage & recovery
diagram.caption: Remember small amounts of task data without promising cloud sync.

title: Build an interactive planner
summary: Connect state, rendering, and persistence in a useful small app.
points: Keep the task array as the source of truth. Render from it after successful add, complete, undo, and delete actions.
Validate titles and assign stable IDs before adding a task. Treat stored and fetched text as untrusted input when rendering.
Keep filters as views: showing only completed tasks must not discard unfinished tasks from the saved array.
Announce outcomes and preserve useful keyboard focus after a task disappears. Test empty, long-text, filtered, and error states.

The downloadable starter has working add, complete, delete, filters, reload persistence, and a local JSON ideas request. Extend it with editing and a due-date feature; document the browser-only storage limit.
output:
1 2
Filtering computes a view without discarding the completed task.
mistake: Saving only the visible filtered tasks loses the tasks hidden by the filter.
challenge: Extend the starter with an edit action and due dates. Check reload, keyboard-only use, text that looks like HTML, a missing ideas file, and unavailable storage.

diagram.caption: Connect state, rendering, and persistence in a useful small app.
